questions.question: Which actress was born Norma Jeane Mortenson?
questions.fact: She spent much of her childhood in foster homes and an orphanage in Los Angeles before becoming one of the biggest stars of the 1950s.

questions.question: Who was nicknamed "the Maid of Orléans"?
questions.fact: She was only about 19 when she was burned at the stake in Rouen in 1431. The Catholic Church made her a saint in 1920.

questions.question: Who was known as "the Lady with the Lamp"?
questions.fact: She was also a gifted statistician who used a pie-chart-like "rose diagram" to show that most soldiers were dying of disease, not wounds.

questions.question: Who said "Veni, vidi, vici" (I came, I saw, I conquered)?
questions.fact: He reportedly wrote it in a message to Rome after a lightning victory at Zela, in modern Turkey, in 47 BC.

questions.question: Which US president said "Ask not what your country can do for you"?
questions.fact: It comes from his 1961 inaugural speech. At 43 he was the youngest person ever elected US president.

questions.question: Who told Parliament in 1940, "I have nothing to offer but blood, toil, tears and sweat"?
questions.fact: Churchill was also a prolific writer: he won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1953.

questions.question: Who reached the top of Everest with Tenzing Norgay in 1953?
questions.fact: Hillary was a beekeeper from New Zealand, and his face appears on the country's five-dollar note.

questions.question: Who was the first African American president of the United States?
questions.fact: Years earlier he had been the first black president of the Harvard Law Review, after working as a community organiser in Chicago.

questions.question: Which talk-show host grew up in poverty in rural Mississippi before building a media empire?
questions.fact: By her own account, she sometimes wore dresses made from potato sacks as a child. She became one of the world's first black billionaires.

questions.question: Who founded Amazon in his garage in 1994?
questions.fact: He left a well-paid Wall Street job to start Amazon. In 2021 he flew to the edge of space on a rocket from his own company, Blue Origin.

questions.question: Which entrepreneur founded the Virgin group?
questions.fact: He struggled at school with dyslexia, left as a teenager, and started Virgin as a mail-order record business in 1970.

questions.question: Who co-founded Apple with Steve Jobs in 1976?
questions.fact: Wozniak hand-built Apple's first computer, the Apple I, which went on sale for the odd price of $666.66.

questions.question: Who founded the rocket company SpaceX in 2002?
questions.fact: Born in Pretoria, South Africa, he sold his first video game, a space shooter called Blastar, when he was 12.

questions.question: Which Spanish conquistador brought down the Aztec Empire?
questions.fact: He was born in Medellín, in Extremadura, the same region of Spain as Francisco Pizarro, who conquered the Inca.

questions.question: Who received the first US patent for the telephone, in 1876?
questions.fact: Bell reportedly thought people should answer the phone with "Ahoy!". Edison's choice, "Hello", won.

questions.question: Which Austrian composer wrote his first pieces at about the age of five?
questions.fact: He wrote over 600 works before dying at just 35, including operas such as "The Magic Flute" and "Don Giovanni".

questions.question: Which physicist wrote the bestseller "A Brief History of Time"?
questions.fact: He was diagnosed with motor neurone disease at 21 and given about two years to live. He lived to 76.

questions.question: Which silent-film star created the character of "the Tramp"?
questions.fact: He grew up in deep poverty in London and spent time in a workhouse as a child before becoming one of the richest stars in Hollywood.

questions.question: Which singer was nicknamed "the King of Pop"?
questions.fact: He was the youngest of the Jackson 5 and sang lead on their first US number one, "I Want You Back", at the age of 11.

questions.question: Which wrestler-turned-actor is nicknamed "The Rock"?
questions.fact: He has said he had just $7 to his name after being cut from a Canadian football team, and named his company Seven Bucks Productions.

questions.question: Which basketball legend was nicknamed "His Airness"?
questions.fact: He was left off his high-school varsity team as a sophomore, which he later said pushed him to work even harder.

questions.question: Which tennis star won 23 Grand Slam singles titles, an Open Era record for women?
questions.fact: She won the 2017 Australian Open while about eight weeks pregnant with her daughter.

questions.question: Which footballer scored the "Hand of God" goal?
questions.fact: Maradona led Argentina to win that 1986 World Cup, and in Spain he played for both Barcelona and Sevilla.

questions.question: According to legend, who shouted "Eureka!" in the bath?
questions.fact: The Roman writer Vitruvius tells the story: he worked out how to test a king's gold crown and ran home through Syracuse without his clothes.

questions.question: Who led the first expedition to reach the South Pole, in 1911?
questions.fact: The Norwegian's team, using sled dogs, arrived about five weeks before Scott's British party.

questions.question: What was Freddie Mercury's birth name?
questions.fact: He was born in 1946 in Zanzibar, now part of Tanzania, and spent much of his childhood at a boarding school in India.

questions.question: Which singer's real name is Reginald Dwight?
questions.fact: He took "Elton" from saxophonist Elton Dean and "John" from blues singer Long John Baldry, both bandmates of his.

questions.question: What was Muhammad Ali's name when he won Olympic gold?
questions.fact: He won light-heavyweight gold at the 1960 Rome Olympics, aged 18, and changed his name in 1964.

questions.question: Which jazz trumpeter was nicknamed "Satchmo"?
questions.fact: He grew up poor in New Orleans and learned to play the cornet in a home for troubled boys.

questions.question: Which Spanish striker is nicknamed "El Niño"?
questions.fact: He scored the only goal of the Euro 2008 final against Germany, giving Spain its first major title in 44 years.

questions.question: Which French king was known as "the Sun King"?
questions.fact: His grandson became Philip V, the first Bourbon king of Spain, and King Felipe VI descends from that line.

questions.question: Who said "The only thing we have to fear is fear itself"?
questions.fact: He said it at his first inauguration in 1933, during the Great Depression. He went on to win four presidential elections.

questions.question: Who told Stanford graduates in 2005, "Stay hungry, stay foolish"?
questions.fact: He was quoting the farewell message on the back cover of the last Whole Earth Catalog, a 1970s publication he loved.

questions.question: Who ran the first recorded mile in under four minutes, in 1954?
questions.fact: He was a medical student at the time, ran 3:59.4 at Oxford, and later became a leading neurologist.

questions.question: Who became the first man to win eight Wimbledon singles titles?
questions.fact: He won his eighth title in 2017, aged 35, without dropping a single set all tournament.

questions.question: Which Spanish golfer won the Open Championship three times?
questions.fact: By his own account, he learned the game as a boy on the beaches of Pedreña, Cantabria, with an old 3-iron.

questions.question: Which Spanish cyclist won five Tours de France in a row, from 1991 to 1995?
questions.fact: His resting heart rate was reportedly as low as about 28 beats per minute, less than half that of a typical adult.

questions.question: Which milkshake-machine salesman turned the McDonald brothers' burger stand into a global chain?
questions.fact: He was 52 when he met Richard and Mac McDonald in 1954, and he later bought them out.

questions.question: Which comedian's family lived in a van for a time when he was a teenager?
questions.fact: By his own account, he wrote himself a $10 million cheque for "acting services rendered" while broke, and soon earned that much for a film.

questions.question: Which Swedish entrepreneur started out selling matches as a boy and later founded IKEA?
questions.fact: He founded IKEA in 1943 at just 17, and stayed famous for his frugal habits, like flying economy, even as a billionaire.

questions.question: Which French designer spent part of her childhood in an orphanage before building a fashion empire?
questions.fact: Her real first name was Gabrielle. "Coco" reportedly came from songs she sang in cafés as a young woman.

questions.question: Which Florentine wrote "The Prince", a famous guide to power?
questions.fact: He wrote it in 1513, soon after being jailed and tortured when the Medici family returned to power in Florence.

questions.question: Which Roman emperor wrote the Stoic classic "Meditations"?
questions.fact: He wrote it in Greek as private notes to himself, often while on military campaigns. He probably never meant it to be published.

questions.question: Which Stoic philosopher was born in Córdoba?
questions.fact: He was tutor and adviser to the emperor Nero, who later ordered him to take his own life, in AD 65.

questions.question: Who became Spain's first democratically elected prime minister after Franco, in 1977?
questions.fact: During the 1981 coup attempt in parliament, he was one of very few MPs who stayed in their seat while shots were fired.

questions.question: Which Spanish scientist won the 1906 Nobel Prize for his work on nerve cells?
questions.fact: He is called the father of modern neuroscience, and his detailed drawings of brain cells are still printed in textbooks.

questions.question: Which actress won a record four Best Actress Oscars?
questions.fact: She famously didn't attend the ceremony for any of her four wins.

questions.question: Which two Spanish tenors sang alongside Pavarotti as "The Three Tenors"?
questions.fact: Their first concert was in Rome on the eve of the 1990 World Cup final, partly to celebrate Carreras's recovery from leukaemia.

questions.question: Which Catalan chef ran elBulli, often called the world's best restaurant?
questions.fact: Restaurant magazine named elBulli the world's best restaurant five times, and it opened only about six months a year.

questions.question: In 2024, which Manchester City midfielder became the first Spanish man since 1960 to win the Ballon d'Or?
questions.fact: The previous Spanish-born winner was Luis Suárez Miramontes, Barcelona's Galician playmaker, in 1960.

questions.question: Who was the first gymnast to be awarded a perfect 10 at the Olympics, in 1976?
questions.fact: She was 14. The scoreboard couldn't show 10.00, so it displayed "1.00" instead.

questions.question: Who wrote "I think, therefore I am"?
questions.fact: He first wrote it in French, "Je pense, donc je suis", in 1637, before the Latin version "cogito, ergo sum" became famous.

questions.question: "Let them eat cake" is famously but wrongly pinned on which queen?
questions.fact: Rousseau wrote of "a great princess" saying it in his "Confessions", when Marie Antoinette was still a child in Austria.

questions.question: What is Pelé's real first name?
questions.fact: He got the nickname "Pelé" as a schoolboy and, by his own account, never found out what it meant.

questions.question: Which Madrid-born philosopher wrote "Those who cannot remember the past are condemned to repeat it"?
questions.fact: Born in Madrid in 1863, he moved to the USA as a boy, wrote in English and taught philosophy at Harvard.

questions.question: Who was the first woman to win the Nobel Peace Prize, in 1905?
questions.fact: She briefly worked as Alfred Nobel's secretary and stayed friends with him; she is thought to have inspired the peace prize.

questions.question: Which Spanish politician led the fight for women's right to vote in 1931?
questions.fact: Spanish women first voted in a general election in 1933, two years after she won the debate in parliament.

questions.question: Which billionaire sold fax machines door to door before founding Spanx?
questions.fact: By her own account, she started the company with $5,000 of savings and kept her day job while building it.

questions.question: Which Roman emperor was born in Itálica, near modern Seville?
questions.fact: He was the first emperor born outside Italy, and the Roman Empire reached its greatest size under his rule.

questions.question: Which Spanish engineer invented the autogiro, a forerunner of the helicopter?
questions.fact: His autogiro made its first successful flight in January 1923 at Getafe, near Madrid.
